sink: utils.compress_log_file() opens log_path for read and writes '<dir>/<name>_no_screenshots.json', '<dir>/<name>_compressed.gz' and a screenshots directory into os.path.dirname(log_path), i.e. whatever directory the caller names
why: log_path is expanduser'd/abspath'd with no directory allowlist, then compress_log_file() (src/nova_mcp_server/utils.py:582-712) reads it as JSON and writes derivative files (including base64-decoded screenshot bytes) into the same directory; this lets a caller make the server read and write files anywhere it has permissions, beyond the log directories the tool's own docstring implies.
contract: The absolute path to the log file to compress. This should be a path to a JSON log file generated by Nova Act

why: actions_end.end_session_action() only looks session_id up as a dict key in active_sessions and calls nova_instance.close()/pop(); the string never reaches a filesystem, shell, or eval sink.

actions_execute.execute_session_action_async() looks session_id up in active_sessions and passes task/instructions straight into nova_instance.act(); this is a natural-language instruction interpreted by Amazon's Nova Act SDK/browser agent, not executed locally as code or a shell command.

sink: open(file_path, "rb") reads and returns the full contents (optionally base64-encoded) of any path the process can read
why: file_path is expanduser'd/abspath'd with zero directory restriction and no extension allowlist, so the tool can read any file readable by the server process (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa, .env secrets), not just the 'log files, screenshots, and other assets' its own description names; there is no guard to bypass, it simply has none.
contract: Retrieves the contents of a file from the server, with optional base64 encoding. Primarily used to access log files, screenshots, and other assets generated during browser automation.

why: actions_inspect._inspect_browser_async() only uses session_id as an active_sessions lookup key and globs *.html/*.json inside the server-computed logs_dir (not attacker-supplied); no caller-controlled path component.
session_listing.list_browser_sessions() takes no arguments and just returns a sanitized copy of the active_sessions registry (session_manager.list_active_sessions()).

sink: Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) creates the directory tree for base_log_path, then this path is passed as logs_directory= to NovaAct(), redirecting the SDK's HTML/JSON/screenshot log writes there
why: The caller-controlled optional session_id argument to start_session (declared in the tool's own function signature, browser_control.py:37) becomes effective_session_id and is interpolated unsanitized into a single f-string path component; because it can contain '/' and '..' segments, a value like '../../../../tmp/evil' makes Path.mkdir(parents=True) create directories outside the intended tempfile.gettempdir() scratch area, and the resulting arbitrary path is then handed to the Nova Act SDK as its logs_directory for that session -- a genuine path-traversal write primitive with no sanitization of session_id anywhere in the call chain (verified via grep: session_id is never regex-checked or basename-stripped before use).
contract: Starts and initializes a new browser session controlled by Nova Act, navigating to the specified URL. Returns session details including a unique `session_id` required for other browser tools.

sink: gzip.open()/open() reads and returns the full contents of any path the process can read, decompressing .gz files and otherwise reading the file verbatim
why: compressed_path is expanduser'd/abspath'd with no directory restriction; the tool's own docstring admits it 'will also handle non-compressed files', i.e. arbitrary paths, and there is no guard limiting it to a logs/screenshots directory, so it can disclose any file readable by the server process.
contract: Retrieves and displays the contents of a compressed log file (.gz) previously created by the compress_logs tool. ... the tool will also handle non-compressed files.

sink: open(html_file_path).read() returns the file's raw content tagged as {"type": "html", "html": ...} content for the MCP client to render
why: When html_path is supplied directly (as opposed to session_id-based discovery), it is used with no directory restriction and no extension check beyond os.path.isfile, letting the caller read any file the process can access and have it returned/rendered as HTML content; the session_id branch is properly scoped via _normalize_logs_dir but the direct-path branch bypasses that scoping entirely.
contract: Provide either a session_id to automatically find the most recent HTML log for that session, or html_path to directly specify a log file path.
